title: Common-emitter audio amplifier
goal: A reader must be able to trace the input, bias, collector output, and bypass paths of a single-supply NPN common-emitter amplifier without confusing its transistor terminals or junctions.

rubric.must: Q1 is an NPN symbol whose base connects to CIN and the R1/R2 junction, collector connects to RC and COUT, and emitter connects to RE and CE.
R1 connects the 12 V supply to the base and R2 connects the base to ground, with neither resistor bypassed by a wire.
CE and RE form separate parallel branches from the emitter to ground, with CE's positive terminal at the emitter and no direct wire joining the emitter to the base.
The input reaches the base through CIN, and the collector reaches the grounded RL load through COUT, with neither coupling capacitor shorted by a wire.
Joined wire branches have visible junction dots, and crossings between separate nets do not look like joined branches.

Labels beside their respective symbols clearly show Q1 as 2N3904, V1 as 12 V, R1 as 47 kΩ, R2 as 10 kΩ, RC as 4.7 kΩ, RE as 1 kΩ, CE as 100 µF, CIN as 1 µF, COUT as 10 µF, RL as 47 kΩ, and CS as 100 nF.
The supply is above the ground return, all labels are legible without overlaps, and wires avoid component bodies except at their terminals.

ideal.notes: Reviewed. Supply rail across the top, return along the bottom, bias divider on the left, collector branch in the middle, coupling capacitor and load on the right; the transistor's base, collector and emitter are lettered and the bypass capacitor's positive plate faces the emitter.
